To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed neutron multiplicity ratio is in agreement with the corresponding binary mass ratio and the neutron velocity distributions are consistent with isotropic neutron emission from fully accelerated fragments.

(1) the neutron emission from strongly damped reactions is dominated by evaporation from fully accelerated fragments and not by pre-equilibrium or fission processes; (2) the neutron multiplicity is proportional to the mass of the fragment and not to the excitation energy of the fragment; and (3) the neutron emission is isotropic and independent of the fragment velocity.

the neutron multiplicities in strongly damped reactions of /sup 84/Kr on /super 166/Er are consistent with the predictions of statistical-model calculations assuming that the fragments are unpolarized and fully accelerated, and that the ratio of neutron multiplicites for the light and the heavy fragment is equal to the ratio of the corresponding masses.

the observed neutron multiplicities and angular and velocity distributions are fully compatible with a statistical model of neutron evaporation.
the observed neutron emission is a result of statistical decay of fully accelerated fragments.

the neutron multiplicities are not affected by the strong angular momentum dissipation in the entrance channel.
